mechanism.summary: Replace Rc<ObjectData>'s per-object allocator boundary with pointer-sized intrusive strong/weak object cells held in stable Realm-local blocks, and route ordinary constructor receiver allocation through those blocks.
mechanism.generality: Admission depends only on ordinary object allocation in a Realm. It does not inspect JavaScript source, benchmark names, paths, constructor/function names, property names, inputs, iteration counts, or results. Object identity, prototype behavior, descriptors, weak caches, cross-realm construction, and the existing unpooled fallback all use the same handle contract.
semantic_risks: preserving exactly-once ObjectData destruction and strong-count clone/drop behavior
preserving ObjectWeakRef upgrade, clone, and final-drop behavior without resurrecting destroyed object data
keeping arena blocks alive while an escaping Value or weak cache handle remains after its Realm owner drops
preserving stable identity across prototypes, cycles, property caches, descriptor mutation, and cross-realm construction
localizing every raw-pointer validity and slot-reuse proof to the arena implementation

The release binary SHA-256 is 568549b735c590a0787d93a84f67d2f3c65312f917e863714a1bb28e6f757ad4 and is runtime-identical to queue candidate 32a00b0e outside evidence-only commits. profile_evidence.shared_cost: The rank-two 5.351608x QuickJS-NG gap repeatedly creates live ordinary receiver headers through Rc. A Realm-local block allocator removes that system-allocation class even when the objects remain live together, unlike a post-drop reuse cache.
